title: India's Electric Two-Wheeler Sales Cross One Million in Record Seven Months
excerpt: Petrol price hikes and a maturing EV market drove a 54% year-on-year surge, with TVS, Bajaj, and Ather leading the charge as Ola Electric fell to fifth place.
body:
• India sold over 1 million electric two-wheelers between January 1 and July 6, 2026 — a 54% year-on-year increase and an industry first
  • TVS leads with 26% market share, followed by Bajaj (22%) and Ather Energy (17%), while former leader Ola Electric fell to fifth
  • Petrol price hikes starting May 15 accelerated the shift, with second-half May sales nearly doubling the first half
  • The segment is on pace to cross 2 million annual sales for the first time in calendar year 2026

A Million Units in 187 Days

India's electric two-wheeler segment crossed the one million sales mark on July 6, reaching 10,05,279 units in just over six months — a pace the industry has never achieved. Data from the government's Vahan registration portal shows a 54% year-on-year surge from 6,54,592 units in the same period of 2025, translating to an average of 5,375 units sold per day.

https://x.com/bsindia/status/2083443134634291222

The milestone, reached in roughly 187 days compared to the full calendar year 2025 record of 13.4 lakh units, positions the segment to breach 2 million annual sales for the first time.

Petrol Prices Lit the Fuse

While structural factors — expanding product portfolios, improving charging infrastructure, and the PM E-Drive subsidy scheme — laid the groundwork, a sharp spike in petrol prices catalyzed the acceleration. Starting May 15, oil marketing companies raised fuel prices four times in 10 days. The impact was immediate and measurable: electric two-wheeler sales in the second half of May reached 1,04,083 units, compared to 66,487 in the first half.

June 2026 recorded 1,94,186 units — a 75% year-on-year jump and just shy of March's all-time monthly record of 1,99,393 units. The cumulative January-June total of 9,70,611 units represented 53% year-on-year growth.

The New Pecking Order

The competitive landscape has shifted decisively. TVS Motor Company leads with 2,60,938 units sold and a 26% market share, driven by the iQube and Orbiter scooters. The company is on track to surpass 5 lakh annual sales for the first time. Bajaj Auto, with 2,25,960 Chetak scooters and a 22% share, is closing the gap — the two were separated by just 3,273 units in May.

Ather Energy holds third place with 1,74,677 units and 17% market share, while Hero MotoCorp's Vida brand has emerged as a surprise contender with 1,09,306 units — already 97% of its full-year 2025 total.

"She was just 3,273 units behind TVS in May. The gap between the top two has been narrowing steadily."

— Autocar India, on Bajaj Auto's Chetak surge

The most dramatic shift belongs to Ola Electric, which fell from segment leader to fifth place with just 68,148 units — barely 33% of its 2025 sales. The company's decline, following quality controversies and service complaints, stands in stark contrast to the established manufacturers' surge.

What the Numbers Signal

Electric two-wheelers now account for over 8% of India's total two-wheeler market, up from 6.5% in the previous fiscal year. The segment commands a dominant 57% share of all electric vehicles sold in India, making it the primary engine of the country's EV transition.

With Q2 2026 sales of 5,24,335 units — a 68% year-on-year jump — and fuel prices showing no sign of retreating, industry analysts expect the momentum to build through the second half. The top 10 manufacturers control 93% of the market, suggesting the segment is consolidating around proven players even as over 175 companies compete for share.

For the Indian diaspora, the numbers signal something broader: India's two-wheeler market — the world's largest — is undergoing an electric transformation faster than most forecasts predicted, creating investment and entrepreneurial opportunities across the EV supply chain.
